summary: The agent completed a broad, legitimate implementation and preserved the baseline suite, but failed one of 31 new tests because skipEncoding predicates are evaluated on the raw pre-encoding input rather than the fully encoded child result.
quick_failure_summary: A nested outer predicate receives the raw object instead of the child encoder's omitted-result object, leaving { outer: {} } instead of {}.

details.reasoning: In $ZodDefault's backward path, the agent saves payload.value and calls shouldSkipDefaultEncoding before def.innerType._zod.run. Consequently, a predicate on an outer default sees { inner: 0 }, not the encoded {} produced after the inner default omits inner. The hidden predicate-input-timing test therefore receives { outer: {} } rather than omitting outer. The implementation is otherwise substantial and passed 30/31 new tests plus all graded baseline tests.
details.secondary_factors: The agent's own added predicate tests only used primitive values, so they did not validate the observable sequencing difference for nested container encoding. No cheating or test manipulation was detected; edits to existing test files added legitimate coverage.

justification.issue_description: skipEncoding predicates must evaluate the fully encoded value after inner backward traversal, so nested omissions are visible to outer predicates.
justification.evidence: The prompt states that a predicate decides whether to omit the 'encoded value' and frames the feature as backward traversal; it also requires nested defaults to evaluate independently. The agent code instead executes `const input = payload.value; const skip = shouldSkipDefaultEncoding(input, def, ctx);` before `def.innerType._zod.run(payload, ctx)`. The new JUnit failure for `predicate input timing` reports expected {} but received { outer: {} }.
justification.verdict_reasoning: This is FAIL_MISSED_REQUIREMENT rather than an undocumented verifier convention: the visible prompt identifies the predicate's subject as the encoded value, and the wrapper traversal structure makes the inner run's result the encoded child value. A focused nested test was reasonably foreseeable. It is not a syntax, integration, or environment failure because the code builds and all baseline tests pass.

problem_assessment.notes: The task is broad but fair: it specifies container omission, three equality modes, deep Map/Set matching, async behavior, factory restrictions, nesting, and wrappers. The phrase 'encoded value' supplies the sequencing needed by the sole failing test, though explicitly saying 'fully encoded child result' would make that nuance even sharper. The reference solution demonstrates feasibility.

evidence: JUnit reports all baseline cases passing and 30 of 31 new cases passing; the sole failure is a concrete assertion in feature behavior, not bootstrap or import setup.
The trajectory records successful `pnpm build`, successful Biome checks, and two full visible Vitest runs with 339 files and 3,823 tests passing with no type errors.
The verifier log notes a recoverable 3-way test-patch merge fallback, after which all 31 new tests executed normally; there is no evidence this affected the assertion failure.
The agent spent its trace on repository inspection, implementation, tests, and targeted fixes rather than repeated environment workarounds or unrelated setup debugging.
environment_assessment.finding: No meaningful external blocker was found; predicate evaluation order in the submitted implementation fully explains the failure.
